page.layout: One page of text. At the top: printed page number 74, a running head, and a printer's ornament. Below it, a four-line Latin epigram with the signature T. A. C. Then a title in two lines, a large initial R, and a verse poem in italic with the signature I. E. B. No margin notes.

p.i: REge, foret cum de Francùm viuente, Corona Alta instituta quaestio: Et cupidus guttam Regalis sanguinis in se Non repperiret Guysius: Romulea nodum, ceu Gordius, arte LIGAVIT Ad Cardines Lutetia, Hoc vt Regalis posthac successio nodo, Non censeatur sanguine, Vidit id Henricus: Regali at soluere in urbe Haud tutum erat, vult Blasiis. Hic pleno nodum confessu in pectore Guysî Rex soluit ense Gordium, Gaude, Borbonius sanguis, quo Francia censet Successionem Regiam.

page.notes: The line "torsit & vnda" is cut off at the outer edge of the scan; "vnda" is uncertain. The small caps in the heading "LIGA SOLVTA BLÆSIIS CÆDE." and the initial R are read from the scan. Lines of the poem are run together within one paragraph as one stanza; the printed line breaks are kept by the order of the words, not as separate lines. Printed spelling is kept, including "Guysius", "Lutetia," and "Guysî". No printing errors were corrected.
